children: The New York Federal Reserve said that Australia's ANZ Group
has been dropped from its list of foreign exchange counterparties.
ANZ's removal leaves the Commonwealth Bank of Australia
as the only Australian lender on its list of 21 banks that are used in foreign exchange operations on behalf of the Federal Reserve and the US Treasury.
The New York Fed did not give a reason for ANZ's removal, which was effective November 25, according to its website.
ANZ, the smallest of Australia's "Big Four" lenders by market capitalisation, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
To be eligible as a counterparty, banks must meet requirements that include having a substantial presence as market makers providing two-way liquidity in foreign exchange markets, the website said.
They must also have back-office operations of sufficient size and experience to confirm and arrange settlement of transactions with the New York Fed, and manage the trading volumes it requires.
"FX counterparties are expected to continue to meet these expectations and eligibility requirements on an ongoing basis," the website said.
The last bank to be dropped was Credit Suisse in September 2023, according to the website, months after it collapsed and was sold to rival UBS in a rescue deal.
